_test_case_note:
TC4 (v0.0.2) -- METRICS ON. The 'ON' half of a matched pair with metaflow_testing/v0_0_2_tc5_metrics_off.json. OBJECTIVE: functional parity + performance comparison across the two telemetry modes. The pair must be read together; neither file means anything on its own.

THE ONLY INTENDED DIFFERENCE IS TELEMETRY. This file sets reconciliation_flows[0].logging_config to {run_log_capture: true, mismatch_log_capture: true}; TC5 sets both to false. Flow structure, flow count, source_type, cdc_load_strategy on every flow, source_config shape, json_string_columns schema_ddl, transformation_sql, match_keys, compare_columns, comparison_direction, execution_mode and error_handling are byte-for-byte the same in both files apart from the identifier/table renames described next. Any other divergence confounds the comparison and invalidates the run.

WHY THE IDENTIFIERS AND TARGETS DIFFER (this is required, not a divergence): dataflow_group_id, every dataflow_id/flow_step_id/reconciliation_id, every target_schema and every target_table are distinct between TC4 and TC5. The control tables (metaflow.config.dataflow_group_spec / ingestion_flow_spec / transformation_flow_spec / reconciliation_flow_spec) are keyed on those ids, and a Lakeflow dataset has exactly one owning pipeline -- so sharing them would make the second onboarding MERGE over the first's rows and make the two pipelines fight over the same tables' transaction logs. The two runs would then overwrite each other's results and there would be nothing left to compare. TC4 owns the *_tc4_* ids and the bronze_tc4_metrics / silver_tc4_metrics / recon_tc4_metrics schemas; TC5 owns the *_tc5_* ids and the bronze_tc5_metrics / silver_tc5_metrics schemas.

THE ACTUAL ASSERTION IS A CROSS-TARGET COMPARISON, NOT AN IN-SPEC ONE. Nothing inside this spec proves parity. After both jobs have run, compare the two target tables directly:
  - row counts equal: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM metaflow.bronze_tc4_metrics.tc4_customer_primary) AS tc4, (SELECT count(*) FROM metaflow.bronze_tc5_metrics.tc5_customer_primary) AS tc5;
  - same for tc4_customer_replica vs tc5_customer_replica and for the silver payload tables tc4_customer_payload_json vs tc5_customer_payload_json;
  - data consistency: an EXCEPT in both directions over the business columns (customer_id, customer_name, status, payload_tier, payload_score) between metaflow.silver_tc4_metrics.tc4_customer_payload_json and metaflow.silver_tc5_metrics.tc5_customer_payload_json must return zero rows both ways. Exclude the __framework_* technical columns from that EXCEPT -- ingestion timestamps and run ids legitimately differ between two separate runs and are not part of the parity claim.

WHERE THE DURATION/LATENCY NUMBERS COME FROM -- NOT FROM THIS SPEC. This spec deliberately declares no timing mechanism; inventing one inside the pipeline would itself add overhead and bias the very measurement it is trying to take. Read the durations from the platform's own run history:
  - Jobs run history for 'Metaflow Test v0.0.2 - TC4 Metrics ON Batch Recon Pipeline' vs '... TC5 Metrics OFF ...' (Workflows > job > Runs gives per-task duration, so the run_<slug>_pipeline task can be isolated from setup/seed/onboard);
  - system.lakeflow.job_run_timeline and system.lakeflow.job_task_run_timeline for the same two job ids (period_start_time/period_end_time), which is the queryable form of the same data and the one to use for repeated trials;
  - the pipeline update's own event log for per-flow latency (the update's flow_progress events).
Compare the run_<slug>_pipeline task duration only. The telemetry overhead being measured is the cost of TC4's reconciliation_run_log / reconciliation_mismatch_log writes, which happen inside that pipeline update; the setup, seed and onboard tasks are identical work in both jobs and including them only dilutes the signal. Run both jobs at least twice and compare medians -- a single serverless run's start-up variance is larger than the effect being measured.

WHY THERE IS NO dq_config ON THE RECONCILIATION FLOW IN EITHER FILE. Under the v1.7.3 logging contract, dq_config.rules on a pipeline-mode reconciliation flow attach dlt expectations to the recon__*__metrics dataset, which is only registered when run_log_capture resolves true. TC5, which must have both flags false, is therefore forbidden from carrying dq_config.rules at all (spec_validator.py::_validate_logging_config rejects it). TC4 could legally carry them -- but if it did, the pair would differ in expectation evaluation as well as in log writes, and the measured duration delta would no longer be attributable to telemetry alone. So dq_config is omitted from BOTH reconciliation flows on purpose. For the same reason neither file uses execution_mode 'pipeline_audit_only': that mode with both flags resolving false is rejected outright (it would register compute with no output), so TC5 could not mirror it and both files use 'pipeline'.

WHY THE RECON SOURCE IS THE APPEND TABLE AND THE CDC TABLE IS THE COMPARE TARGET. execution_mode 'pipeline' puts this flow's L3/L4/L5 datasets inside this group's own pipeline update, and V-CYC-7 requires the reconciliation SOURCE to be produced by an append-only producer (SCD1/SCD2/SCD3/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC all dispatch through dlt.apply_changes, i.e. real MERGE writes, and are rejected as a recon source in pipeline mode). So the APPEND streaming table is the source and the SCD1 CDC table is the compared target -- which is still a CDC reconciliation, and is the only arrangement of these two that pipeline mode accepts. V-CYC-1 is satisfied because the source is this group's own ingestion target. append_target_table points at {{catalog}}.tc4_remediation.tc4_heal_landing: not an in-spec target (V-CYC-2), not this group's raw ingestion source (V-CYC-3/4), and not either compared side (V-CYC-5).

SEEDING. Both jobs seed via notebooks/00_seed_sample_data/02_seed_metaflow_testing_data.py, which lands sample_data/metaflow_testing/excalibur_usecase/autoload_batch1.csv (customer_id, customer_name, status) at /Volumes/{{catalog}}/Excalibur_usecase/landing_autoload/incoming/. Both ingestion flows below read that one landed batch: this is a batch load of two tables from one fixture, so the two tables are identical by construction and the reconciliation has a known-good expected outcome (zero mismatches) in BOTH test cases. That matters -- a parity test whose two halves disagree about the data is not measuring telemetry.

ingestion_flows.source_description: TC4 (metrics ON) table 1 of 2: batch Auto Loader load of the Excalibur customer extract into an APPEND streaming table. This is the reconciliation SOURCE -- it must be append-only, because execution_mode 'pipeline' rejects a MERGE-writing (SCD*/FULL_SNAPSHOT_CDC) producer as a recon source under V-CYC-7. Structurally identical to v0_0_2_tc5_metrics_off.json's df_tc5_customer_primary_ingest apart from the target schema/table rename.

TC4 (metrics ON) table 2 of 2: the SAME landed batch loaded a second time under an SCD1 CDC strategy (dlt.apply_changes keyed on customer_id), giving the pair a genuine CDC target for the reconciliation to compare against. Because both tables derive from one fixture, the expected recon outcome is zero mismatches in BOTH test cases -- the comparison between TC4 and TC5 is then about telemetry cost, not about differing data.

transformation_flows.source_description: TC4 (metrics ON): SQL transformation that builds a JSON payload string per customer and then parses it back to a NATIVE STRUCT (from_json with an explicit schema), so the silver table carries payload_tier/payload_score as real typed columns rather than an opaque string. Appended to Delta. Identical SQL and identical column set in v0_0_2_tc5_metrics_off.json.
transformation_flows.transformation_sql: SELECT customer_id, customer_name, status, from_json(to_json(struct(CASE WHEN status = 'ACTIVE' THEN 'GOLD' ELSE 'STANDARD' END AS tier, length(customer_name) AS score)), 'tier STRING, score INT').tier AS payload_tier, from_json(to_json(struct(CASE WHEN status = 'ACTIVE' THEN 'GOLD' ELSE 'STANDARD' END AS tier, length(customer_name) AS score)), 'tier STRING, score INT').score AS payload_score FROM tc4_primary_stream

reconciliation_flows._flag_note: THE ONE INTENDED DIFFERENCE FROM TC5. Both capture flags are TRUE here, so the recon__*__metrics dataset is registered and reconciliation_run_log / reconciliation_mismatch_log rows are written on every update. In v0_0_2_tc5_metrics_off.json this same block is {run_log_capture: false, mismatch_log_capture: false} -- silent, which is the v1.7.3 default. The duration delta between the two jobs' run_<slug>_pipeline tasks is the cost of those writes; read it from the Jobs run history / system.lakeflow.job_task_run_timeline, never from anything declared in this spec. No dq_config here on purpose: TC5 is forbidden from carrying one with both flags false, and adding one to TC4 alone would make the pair differ in expectation evaluation as well as in logging.
reconciliation_flows.transform_sql: SELECT customer_id, customer_name, status, current_timestamp() AS healed_at FROM _reconciliation_unmatched_records
